declared.title: Valuing Happiness is Not a Good Way of Pursuing Happiness, but Prioritizing Positivity is: A Replication Study.

population: adults, 75% women (N = 683); country not given in the abstract (a Belgian journal)

findings.text: People who organize their days around pleasant moments (prioritizing positivity) report more happiness, life satisfaction and well-being, and less depression

support.sentence: Regression analyses showed that prioritizing positivity was positively associated with subjective happiness, life satisfaction and psychological well-being, but that it was negatively linked to depression.

findings.text: Valuing happiness went partly the other way: with lower well-being on some measures

support.sentence: Opposite results partly emerged for valuing happiness.

limits: « partly »: the abstract does not say on which of the four measures valuing happiness went with worse scores
